en: Lightning strikes the Earth about 100 times every single second, which adds up to roughly 8 million strikes per day.
The fastest winds on Earth occur inside tornadoes, which can reach incredible speeds of over 480 kilometers per hour.
Antarctica is technically the world's largest desert because it receives less than 200 millimeters of precipitation every single year.
It takes nature up to one thousand years to create just one single inch of fertile topsoil.
Pumice is a unique volcanic rock full of air bubbles, making it the only type of rock that floats on water.
Groundwater holds about thirty percent of Earth's fresh water, while all lakes and rivers hold less than one percent.
Venus spins backward so slowly that one single day on its surface is actually longer than its entire year.
Saturn is so incredibly light that if you could find a bathtub big enough, the entire planet would float in water.
Pulsars are rapidly spinning neutron stars that beam radio waves, rotating up to 716 times every single second.
The Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth at a steady rate of about 3.8 centimeters every single year.
The 1883 eruption of Mount Krakatoa was so loud that it ruptured the eardrums of sailors forty miles away.
In the deep ocean, tsunamis can travel as fast as a commercial jet plane at speeds up to 800 kilometers per hour.
